subject: Can production of NaNs during creation of capture history be caused by low sample size?

messages.author: a254a67210d4345e
messages.subject: Can production of NaNs during creation of capture history be caused by low sample size?
parts:
Hello,

I've got a trapping grid which had 36 captures over three years. When I create my capture history 
willcapturedata<-make.capthist(EDF,trapfile,fmt="trapID",noccasions = 6)
It seems ok, but if I run the summary, it produces NaNs.
Counts by occasion 
                   1  2  3  4  5  6 Total
n                  2  3  0  0  0  0     5
u                  2  3  0  0  0  0     5
f                  5  0  0  0  0  0     5
M(t+1)             2  5  5  5  5  5     5
losses             0  0  0  0  0  0     0
detections         2  3  0  0  0  0     5
detectors visited  2  3  0  0  0  0     5
detectors used    50 50 50 50 50 50   300

Warning message:
In sqrt((temp[2] + temp[3])/(temp[1] - 1)) : NaNs produced

I'm assuming that this is a sample size issue, since I was not catching very many animals? 
I could not find any issues with the data, or code,so I was wondering if anybody else has experienced this?
Thanks.

Lauren

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Can production of NaNs during creation of capture history be caused by low sample size?
parts:
Yes.  The warning is from RPSV that is called by summary.capthist (for reasons I can't remember). You should be able to reproduce it with RPSV( willcapturedata). A dataset with no recaptures is not usable for capture-recapture. P.S. Your subject line is misleading - the warning does not happen during the creation of capture histories. I assume 'trapfile' was a traps object not a file.
Murray
